definitions.explanation: A traditional ceremony in which a newborn baby is brought to a Shinto shrine for the first time, typically around one month after birth, to pray for the child's health and protection.

examples.japanese: ⟦{赤|あか}ちゃん→赤ちゃん：01282_akachan⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{初宮参|はつみやまい}り⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{行|い}った→行く：00119_iku⟧。
examples.english: We went for the baby's first shrine visit.

examples.japanese: {初宮参|はつみやまい}り⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{家族|かぞく}→家族：00552_kazoku⟧⟦{全員|ぜんいん}→全員：03310_zenin⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{正装|せいそう}→正装：16053_seisou⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: The whole family dressed formally for the baby's first shrine visit.

examples.japanese: ⟦{祖母|そぼ}→祖母：00813_sobo⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{赤|あか}ちゃん→赤ちゃん：01282_akachan⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{抱|だ}いて→抱く：02131_daku⟧{初宮参|はつみやまい}り⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧、⟦{昔|むかし}→昔：01515_mukashi⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{習|なら}わし→習わし：13910_narawashi⟧だ。
examples.english: It is a longstanding custom for the grandmother to hold the baby during the first shrine visit.

notes:
A compound of ⟦{初|はつ}→初：10632_hatsu⟧ (first), {宮|みや} (shrine), and {参|まい}り (visit, pilgrimage). Also commonly called ⟦お{宮参|みやまい}り→お宮参り：05925_omiyamairi⟧.

Traditionally performed on the 31st or 32nd day after birth for boys, and the 32nd or 33rd day for girls, though modern families are more flexible with timing. The baby is typically dressed in a white inner garment (⟦{白|しろ}い→白い：00587_shiroi⟧⟦{着物|きもの}→着物：01309_kimono⟧) with a formal outer robe ({祝|いわい}{着|ぎ}), and a Shinto priest performs a blessing.

This is one of the major life-cycle rituals (⟦{通過儀礼|つうかぎれい}→通過儀礼：24879_tsuukagirei⟧) in Japan, along with ⟦{七五三|しちごさん}→七五三：06185_shichigosan⟧ and ⟦{成人式|せいじんしき}→成人式：05494_seijinshiki⟧.

- {初宮参|はつみやまい}り⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{写真|しゃしん}→写真：00753_shashin⟧: first shrine visit photos
- {初宮参|はつみやまい}り⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{着物|きもの}→着物：01309_kimono⟧: shrine visit kimono
- {初宮参|はつみやまい}り⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{祈祷|きとう}→祈祷：22031_kitou⟧: first shrine visit prayer
